title: The autopilot's own work has an end: a definition of done for sprints, retros and the backlog it fills
goal: backlog.py enforces, in check, new and close, and kb-sprint's review and retro steps follow: a sprint gains no item after its start except an S1 bug, and what a review, retro or mid-sprint finding files goes to the backlog as a draft; a finding becomes an item only when it names a failure that happened with its evidence (a commit, a test id or an ops row) and similar finds no near-duplicate, otherwise it is merged into the duplicate's notes or kept in the close commit body only; an item a review or retro filed carries that origin, and a sprint made only of such items has no retro of its own; the number of findings filed per sprint, an item's refused-done and reopen count, the draft inflow against the done outflow of recent sprints and the number of open drafts are capped by the limits its gate sets; the manager stops starting work when no ready item remains, the sprint's budget is spent or an inflow guard trips, and says which in the digest; kb/_self/backlog.md states this as the autopilot's definition of done.

gates.question: This adds a mechanism before a failure it answers has happened (backlog.md, Changing this process). Add it anyway?

What limits does the autopilot keep? Recommended: at most 5 findings filed as items per sprint, an item refused or reopened at most 3 times before it is dropped or escalated, draft inflow no larger than the done outflow of the last 3 sprints, and at most 60 open drafts.
options: 5 findings per sprint, 3 refusals per item, inflow within the last 3 sprints' outflow, 60 open drafts
The operator sets the numbers in each sprint's start gate
No numbers: only the evidence and duplicate rules
gates.recommendation: 5 findings per sprint, 3 refusals per item, inflow within the last 3 sprints' outflow, 60 open drafts
gates.answer: 5 findings per sprint, 3 refusals per item, inflow within the last 3 sprints' outflow, 60 open drafts

gates.question: check, new and close live in bl_check, bl_land and backlog.py, outside this item's touches: bl_bounds puts its rules in front of them at import (the registered handler, and the owning module's cmd_check and cmd_close, become bl_bounds's wrapper). Keep that, or add hook seams in those modules?
options: seams in bl_check, bl_land and backlog.py, in a later item

gates.question: Which sprints does the rule that a running sprint gains no item but an S1 bug hold?
options: only a sprint whose start gate the autopilot answered
gates.recommendation: only a sprint whose start gate the autopilot answered
gates.answer: only a sprint whose start gate the autopilot answered

gates.question: What is the sprint's budget the manager stops on?
options: tokens the sprint's cost report shows

gates.question: Where does an item a review or retro filed carry its origin and evidence, and what does the inflow guard do with no sprint.close row?
options: links origin KIND SP and evidence KIND REF; no close row: the guard does not judge
new item fields, which bl_base owns; no close row: outflow is zero and no finding is filed
gates.recommendation: links origin KIND SP and evidence KIND REF; no close row: the guard does not judge
gates.answer: links origin KIND SP and evidence KIND REF; no close row: the guard does not judge

notes: The failure it answers: closing a sprint turns every accepted review or retro finding into a story, so one sprint's close filed ten drafts (SP-x2pvljz6) and another six (SP-5cwekumc), with the operator as the only brake; an autopilot that answers for the operator has no brake. The existing process rule (backlog.md, Changing this process: a new mechanism only for a failure that happened) becomes a check. The limits gate holds the numbers. The story is large: /kb-item splits it into tasks (what a sprint gains and what findings file; the caps and the inflow guard; the manager's stop conditions and the docs).
